description: Somos estudiantes de Ingeniería de Sistemas e Informática apasionados por el código limpio y el desarrollo ágil. En Control+Z transformamos problemas complejos en software simple, robusto y funcional.
summary: We developed The Earth Information Jukebox, an interactive 3D platform that sonifies NASA satellite data streams into dynamic, evolving electronic House music in real time. The project directly tackles a major barrier in scientific communication: according to the World Health Organization (WHO), at least 2.2 billion people live with vision impairments, meaning traditional visual maps and color-coded climate dashboards systematically exclude blind and low-vision individuals from understanding planetary health. While traditional data sonification tools rely on static midi beeps or pre-recorded audio loops, our platform introduces a zero-latency Web Audio synthesis engine combined with a 3D WebGL globe. By clicking or navigating coordinates on Earth, the system samples high-definition NASA scientific visualization video feeds using a 5x5 spatial matrix kernel, extracting brightness, RGB balance, and chromatic density to synthesize rhythm, chords, basslines, and spatial stereo panning on the fly. Each planetary layer (active wildfires from VIIRS, wetland methane, ocean temperatures, atmospheric CO2, near-surface ozone, and precipitation) maps to a curated House subgenre (Acid, Deep, Afro, Tech, Minimal, Melodic Liquid). This transforms complex Earth science into an inclusive, emotive, and intuitive auditory experience, democratizing space data for schools, science centers, and visually impaired communities worldwide.
details:
What exactly does it do?

The Earth Information Jukebox is an inclusive, real-time climate data sonification system. Specifically:

  • Interactive 3D Planetary Sonification: Allows users to explore Earth on a 3D WebGL globe and listen to live environmental data at any latitude and longitude.
  • Algorithmic Musical Synthesis: Synthesizes notes, polyphonic chords, percussion, and modulated synthesizer filters from satellite video streams in real time, without relying on pre-recorded audio files.
  • Multi-Layer Scientific Exploration: Integrates 6 vital NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) datasets representing key planetary health indicators, plus an engine to upload and sonify custom video feeds.
  • Binaural Spatial Orientation: Uses longitude-driven stereo panning (Western hemisphere in the left ear, Eastern hemisphere in the right ear) to help blind users mentally map the globe.
  • Universal Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 Compliant): Features full screen-reader announcements (aria-live), complete keyboard navigation, guided automated exploration, and a Dracula high-contrast palette for low-vision accessibility.

How does it work?

The process follows a real-time 5-stage pipeline:

  1. Satellite Stream Ingestion: High-definition equirectangular scientific visualization videos (2:1 aspect ratio) from NASA's Earth Information Center and Scientific Visualization Studio loop synchronously in the background.
  2. Spherical Coordinate Mapping: When a user selects a location on the 3D globe (via click, touch, keyboard, or auto-tour), latitude and longitude are translated mathematically into 2D equirectangular video pixel coordinates (X,Y)(X, Y)(X,Y).
  3. 5x5 Matrix Kernel Extraction: An HTML5 Canvas 2D engine samples a 25-pixel matrix centered at the selected coordinate, calculating weighted luminance, RGB balance, and chromatic density to smooth out digital noise, cloud glares, and sensor artifacts.
    • Luminance controls octave registers, filter cutoff frequencies, and arpeggiator velocity.
    • Color balance modulates harmonic chord variations and bass distortion.
    • Chromatic density drives percussion complexity and sub-bass presence.
  4. Spatial Audio and Visual Feedback: Soundwaves radiate in real time with stereophonic audio panning, while 3D harmonic sonic rings and coordinate beacons pulse on the globe matching the musical tempo.

What benefits does it have?

  • Social and Inclusivity: Provides genuine multi-sensory scientific access for 2.2 billion blind, visually impaired, or neurodiverse individuals, turning visual-only satellite charts into intuitive auditory landscapes.
  • Environmental and Educational: Enhances human pattern recognition. The human auditory cortex can distinguish subtle shifts in pitch, timbre, and rhythm faster than the eye can identify microscopic pixel shifts in heatmaps, facilitating climate comprehension.
  • Cultural and Technological: Bridges aerospace science and modern electronic music culture, demonstrating that satellite Earth observation data can be engaging, artistic, and scientifically rigorous simultaneously.

What do you hope to achieve?

In the short term, our goal is to deploy The Earth Information Jukebox in science museums, planetariums, and educational centers for the visually impaired as an interactive exhibit for climate education. In the long term, we aim to expand the engine into an open-source real-time sonification API capable of directly ingesting live satellite data feeds (MODIS, VIIRS, PACE, TEMPO, Landsat), empowering educators, researchers, and artists worldwide to hear the pulse of our planet in real time.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, GitHub.
  • Infrastructure and Technological Hosting: GitHub Pages.
  • Audio Engine & Signal Processing: Tone.js (Web Audio API framework), polyphonic synthesis, FM synthesizers, resonant 24dB filters, spatial stereo panners, dynamic limiter.
  • Frontend & UI: HTML5 semantic shell, CSS3 (Modern Glassmorphism, Dracula Theme, custom animations), Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules architecture).
  • 3D Graphics & Visualization: Globe.gl, Three.js (WebGL renderer, ACESFilmic tone mapping, dynamic 3D beacons and harmonic wave rings).
  • Programming Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3, Python (for video dataset optimization and local testing).
  • Data Processing & Media Optimization: FFmpeg (H.264 video compression, stripping audio, 1280x640 equirectangular normalization), WebP generation for instant 0 ms poster previews, HTML5 Canvas 2D ImageData buffer extraction.
  • Audio & Musical Curation: Ableton Live, FL Studio (harmonic scales calibration, BPM tempo matching, House subgenre modeling).
  • Software & Design: Figma (UI/UX wireframes and component architecture), SVG vector design, Chrome DevTools.
  • Hardware: Development workstations, mobile devices, headphones.
  • Data Sources: NASA Earth Information Center (EIC), NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS), NASA Earthdata.
  • Plus: Native bilingual engine (English and Spanish switchable with 1 click), zero external runtime video dependencies (all optimized datasets bundled <35 MB total), offline-first performance, and full WCAG 2.2 compliance.
